- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then gradually converges toward true values — suggest reducing initial forecast peaks.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 51.06, 53.86), model tends to overshoot and stay elevated longer than warranted — apply dampening factor or lagged smoothing to avoid overreaction.
- Model underestimates true values in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window — consider adjusting for mean reversion or adding a downward bias correction near end of horizon.
- Forecast exhibits persistent upward bias in the first 10–15 days, especially when true values show volatility — reduce initial forecast slope or apply exponential decay to recent history.
- Model fails to capture true value drops after spikes — introduce a “recovery lag” heuristic: if true value drops below 50.0, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until stabilization.
- Forecast tends to ignore recent low values in history — incorporate a 3–5 day moving average of recent lows to prevent overconfidence in high forecasts.
